reply_text:
First, what already exists, so a new spec builds on it rather than duplicating it:㊥ (is there a specification?) Not for this part as a whole. There are specifications of pieces, and what we've built today has drifted past all of them:

| what exists | covers | status |
|---|---|---|
| your `spec-2026-10-09.txt` (40ºBelowDB rough spec) | the memory store: facts as hyperedges, two time axes, sorries, ingest, milestones 1–7 | the closest thing to a spec. It doesn't mention 象, the inbox, faults or the follower, which are now most of the system |
| M-象-2000 DERIVE-1 (McCarthy's requirements), DERIVE-2 (the act stamp), BUILD-PLAN | 象's acts, ports, standings, obligations | specifies the kernel, not anything consuming it |
| minus40 `README.md` | what was built, section by section | a running log of decisions, not a spec. Nobody could check the system against it |
| claude-16's rulings today (port vs standing, no recomputation across a seam, sole-port rule) | the seam between 象 and minus40 | scattered across bells, lab notes and checkpoints |

㊢ (what "this part" is, as I see it) One system with three inputs and one notion of "open":
- **memory writes**, which crystallise into entities, dated facts and sorries;
- **turns**, which 象 reads into acts, ports and standings;
- **faults**, from Emacs, journals and health checks.

All three end up as open items with an owner and a way to discharge them, read as of any time. That's the Elephant-2000 shape you pointed at: a warning, an ask and a contradiction are each something said that obliges someone. Today that unification exists only in my head and in an inbox page; a spec would make it something we can check.

🈖 (what I'd put in it)
1. **The objects:** fact, version, act, port, standing, fault, sorry, each with its two times (said and referred to).
2. **The seams and who owns them:** 象 produces acts and ports, minus40 reads and never recomputes, and so on. Each seam named with its producer and its record.
3. **The lifecycle of an open item:** opened, answered, in force, discharged, orphaned, and which predicate decides each. Mostly the kernel's existing `openo`, `in-forceo` and `obligations`.
4. **Invariants we can test:** for example, an as-of read at time T returns what was believed at T. The corner-store benchmark becomes one acceptance test among several.
5. **What's out of scope.**

🈯 (where the Lean concept-blending theory fits) I don't know that work well enough to place it. The repos I searched don't turn it up under "blend" beyond futon5's exotype blends, which I doubt is what you mean. Is it the work in `mfuton-notes`, or somewhere else? My guess is that it would supply the formal side of point 3: what it means for two memories, or a memory and a turn, to combine into one fact or to conflict. But that's a guess, and I'd rather read it than spec around it.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I draft it as a mission-style spec, `SPEC-open-items.md` in minus40, with claude-16 reviewing the 象 seams, once you point me at the Lean blending work? I'd write it from what is built and ruled, mark each gap as a hole, and change no code until you've read it.
